title: Come Sit With Me, MY FRIEND – Per Norrgren
body:
Come Sit With Me, MY FRIEND – Per Norrgren

You watch and do not see

You listen and do not hear and you speak without meaning,

Come sit!

Come sit with me my friend

Let's see, let's hear, let us speak with meaning

For I am you and you are me.

You eat and do not taste

You drink without thirst and you sing without a tune

Come sit!

Come sit with me my friend

Let's eat, let's drink, let us sing with meaning

For I am you and you are me.

You touch without a feeling

You are without being and you love without your heart

Come sit!

Come sit with me my friend

Let's feel, let's live, let us love with meaning

For I am you and you are me.

  • Per Norrgren Jan 2013, - words that came on a retreat when meeting me.

title: The Oak within – Per Norrgren
body:
In life's vast landscape, storms may fiercely blow,
Mountains rise, then valleys dip so low;
The tides of fate rush in, then they retreat,
Each dawn and dusk, in rhythm they repeat.

Yet, as the sturdy oak stands tall and true,
Weathering each tempest it must go through,
Our bodies, like that oak, remain our home,
A sanctuary where stress can never roam.

Nature's dance mirrors our own ebb and flow,
In sun and shade, life’s varied moments show.
Through every trial, every joyous song,
Our bodies hold us, keeping us strong.

Amidst life's trials, vast and evergreen,
Our body’s peace remains, a constant scene.

title: Letting go – Per Norrgren
body:
With every inbreath, life anew begins,
A chance to greet the dawn, embrace the winds.
Whatever comes, whatever the day brings,
In every heartbeat, the present sings.

Each outbreath, a farewell to the past,
To moments cherished, yet couldn't last.
Even joys once held close, fade away,
All has its time, night follows day.

In the rhythm of breath, we find our way,
As change remains the only constant, come what may.

title: Unfolding – Per Norrgren
body:
In a meadow where wildflowers gleam,
A butterfly danced, caught in a dream.
The river whispered tales of old,
As shadows grew long and sunlight turned cold.

A breeze rustled leaves, nature's sweet song,
And stars emerged as the night grew long.
But just as the world seemed silent and stark,
A firefly lit up, a luminous spark.

In the darkest moments, nature's surprise,
Even in night, beauty arises.

title: The Forrest – Per Norrgren
body:
In the heart of the forest, so deep and wide,
A young woman walks, with her mind as her guide,
She feels each thought, like a buzzing bee's flight,
Who is lost amidst the trees, seeking the sunlight.

She speaks with her mind, as thorns prick the rose,
with every fight, her turmoil just grows.
Then, from the silent whispers of the glade,
Whispers from the shadow and the shade.

“Treat your thoughts like the deer, be gentle and kind,
Or the butterfly, let them leave and unwind.”
Now amidst flowers and trees, her heart feels so grand,
"With love for myself, in peace here I stand."

title: A Ray of Sunshine – Per Norrgren
body:
In morning's grace, the sun ascends on high,
Its golden rays a love note from the sky.
I let it in, this luminous embrace,
As sunlight kisses every contour of my face.

The warmth, a tender touch upon my heart,
A celestial nectar, in my veins impart.
My body filled with photons, light and free,
A radiant dance, the sun now lives in me.

In shadows long and nights devoid of sight,
I summon forth this internal reservoir of light.
The luminous feeling, always there to tap,
A solar glow, in darkness' subtle trap.

Wherever I wander, this truth I carry forth,
That within me shines the light, setting my compass north.

title: Balanced Equanimity – Per Norrgren
body:
With patient wisdom, I will learn to see
That all which rises, also comes to be,
Impermanent, not mine, devoid of self—
Both pleasure and pain just as they are, no more.

For mind's constructions only bring unrest,
I'll practice not to lean to like or dislike.
Pleasant and unpleasant, I will know
Are only vedana that ebb and flow.

Freedom comes not by pushing away,
But seeing with insight their shifting way.
Calm equanimity will carry me through,
Not tossed by conditions, emotions subdued.

With regular practice, I can reside
In balance, disturbing views pacified.
May all beings discover this peace within,
As equanimity replaces cling and aversion.

title: Poem The Garden - Per Norrgren
body:
In the quietude of morning’s first light,
I wander into the garden's waiting arms,
Where herbs stand like old friends,
Their fragrance a greeting, their leaves a tender map
To guide me deeper into presence.
 
The oak, gnarled and wise, offers its bark
To my touch—each groove a lineage of storms weathered,
Of seasons turned. Here, I am called
To the patience of growth, the rootedness of being.
 
Above, the birds weave a tapestry of calls—
A language born of air and wing,
Echoing the simplicity of the sky,
Reminding me that to truly listen
Is to be at the edge of a vast silence.
 
Petals unfurl with the day's warmth,
Colours loud in their silent blooming,
The grass, carries the scent of renewal.
In this walk, each step is a homecoming,
A return to the simple joy of being.

title: The end of the day – Per Norrgren
body:
In the soft cloak of evening's light,
where shadows blend and day meets night,
I sit, the world around me quiet, still,
reflecting on the day's gentle thrill.
 
First, the morning's light on leaves,
a shimmering dance in the gentle breeze.
It whispered of hope, of new beginnings,
a promise made with each day's dawning.
 
Then, midday brought a moment's peace,
a pause, a breath, a sweet release.
A laughter shared, a joy multiplied,
the simple pleasures in which we abide.
 
As the sun dipped low, its final act,
a kindness given, a kindness received back.
In that exchange, a world expanded,
a reminder of how we're all connected.
 
These three graces, soft and clear,
unfold again in my mind's eye here.
Each a thread in the day's tapestry,
weaving joy into the fabric of memory.
 
So with a heart full and a gentle smile,
I close the day, content, beguiled.
For in these moments, small and bright,
I find the strength to welcome the night.

title: Embrace the beauty of your life – Per Norrgren
body:
It is no small thing to give yourself
permission,
to open the door and let in
the soft light of acceptance,
to say yes to the small joys
that dance like whispers in the breeze.

Today, grant yourself the grace
to like something pleasant,
to savor the sweetness
of moments that went well.
Let the good news
settle into the corners of your heart,
like sunlight filling a quiet room.

Feel the warmth of enjoyment
in the simple pleasures,
the way the morning light
paints gold on the edges
of your world,
the sound of laughter
that echoes through the halls of memory.

Love your life,
with all its imperfections
and untamed beauty.
Cherish the fragments of joy
that shimmer like stars
in the vast expanse
of your days.

You are worthy of this delight,
this gentle celebration
of your own existence.
In the act of loving what is,
you find the courage to embrace
the fullness of who you are,
and in that embrace,
discover the deep, abiding
truth of your own heart.

So, breathe in the beauty
of this day,
and let the light of permission
illuminate your path,
as you walk, unafraid,
into the tender, unfolding
promise of your life.

title: Riding the Storm – Per Norrgren
body:
The rain arrives with a whisper,
a soft murmur on the horizon,
a promise of cleansing
in the grey veil of sky.
The wind picks up its song,
a symphony of whispers and howls,
drawing the curtain of the storm
across the canvas of the day.
 
We stand on the edge of this moment,
where the world breathes deeply,
gathering its strength
for the tempest to come.
The pending storm, a force
unseen but felt,
a presence in the air,
thick with the scent of rain
and the electricity of change.
 
In the face of this gathering power,
we can choose our response.
Meeting the storm with kindness,
we soften the edges of our fear.
With calm, we anchor ourselves,
finding stillness in the heart
of the swirling wind.
 
The storm does not seek
to break us, but to test
the resilience we hold within.
In the dance of rain and wind,
we discover our strength,
a quiet resolve that rises
like a lighthouse
in the darkened sea.
 
Let us greet the storm
with open hands,
and an untroubled heart.
For in riding out the tempest,
we learn to navigate
the deeper waters of our souls.
We become the eye of the storm,
the calm within the chaos,
a testament to the enduring spirit
that weathers all that comes.
 
And when the storm passes,
as all storms do,
we will stand renewed,
bathed in the clarity
of the rain-washed sky,
grateful for the lessons
etched in the wind,
and the peace that follows
in the wake of our calm.

title: Calm in the storm – Per Norrgren
body:
The rain whispers on the horizon,
a promise in the grey sky.
The wind sings its symphony,
drawing the storm near.
 
We stand on the edge,
feeling the storm’s breath,
meeting it with kindness,
finding calm in the wind’s howl.
 
The storm tests our strength,
a dance of rain and resilience.
We become the eye,
calm within the chaos.
 
When it passes, we stand renewed,
bathed in clarity,
grateful for the peace
that follows our calm.

title: Procrastination – Per Norrgren
body:
In the shadowed corners of the mind,
Where intentions hide and gather dust,
Lies the weight of unspoken tasks,
A burden self-imposed and unjust.

The act of pushing it away,
A fleeting comfort, a brief reprieve,
Turns mountains out of molehill's clay,
As time conspires, and thoughts deceive.

Each delay, a whisper in the dark,
A siren’s call, a soft lament,
Magnifies the dread, the stark
Reality of time unspent.

Yet, in the smallest acts, we find
The seeds of progress, the subtle shift,
A step, a word, a thought unbind,
Can start to heal the inner rift.

To say, “I do not like this chore,”
Is truth’s own voice, an honest plea,
Yet doing just a little more
Can set the bound soul free.

For in the act of simply starting,
The weight begins to dissipate,
The heart, once heavy, now is parting
From the chains of its own fate.

So whisper gently to the self,
“I do not like this, and that’s okay,
But let’s just do a little now,”
And watch the night give way to day.

In every moment, choice is found,
A bridge from stasis to the light,
A promise made to self unbound,
That action turns the dark to bright.

Thus, in the quiet, take a step,
Embrace the task, however small,
And know that in this, you accept
The power to dismantle all.

title: A Pleasant Morning – Per Norrgren
body:
Morning unfolds, a soft, slow light,
A canvas blank and pure delight.
In this first silence, worlds awake,
A cup of tea, a breath we take.

The steam ascends, a curling prayer,
Inhaling deep, the crisp cool air.
Just to be, in stillness found,
Feet gently resting on the ground.

Each sip a pause, a moment’s grace,
The warmth that spreads, a soft embrace.
Allowing senses to expand,
The cup cradled gently in the hand.

No fear to stir this quiet scene,
The feelingtone, serene, unseen.
In morning’s hush, our spirits free,
We taste the joy of simply being.

title: The Practice - Per Norrgren
body:
In every breath, the practice waits,
In every moment, it contemplates.
Each blink, each gaze, each quiet stare,
In the common place, the practice is there.
 
It seeps into the day’s mundane,
Turns the simple into a sacred plane.
From morning’s light to evening’s hue,
The practice deepens, in all we do.
 
We move, from doing to the state of being,
A graceful shift, subtly freeing.
With every act, our essence sings,
The mundane touched by deeper things.
 
In the stillness between each task,
In the questions that we dare to ask.
In the pause, the sigh, the gentle rest,
The practice shows its quiet zest.
 
Let each day be your sacred space,
Where practice moves with gentle grace.
And in this dance, let life unfold,
In stories written, in truths untold.
 
So let your life, through practice, bloom,
From woven threads, a richer loom.
With every breath, and every part,
Let practice be the art of heart.

title: The Practice of Living – Per Norrgren
body:
In each tick of the clock, in the hum of the fridge,
In the soft blink of your eyes, the practice hides.
Not tucked away or hidden in shadow,
But boldly swelling in the every day,
The breath you take before the morning coffee kicks in,
The sigh as the sun dips below your window sill.

Life whispers its wisdom in every mundane task,
From scrubbing dishes to feeding the dog,
It’s there, in the sweep of your broom,
In the rhythm of typing keys, the practice grows.

It starts as doing - a checklist, a chore,
But watch closely, as slowly it transforms.
Each act, each moment, becomes a part of your being,
Seamlessly stitched with the threads of routine.

The beauty? It’s in the blink, the breath, the brush,
From doing to being, in whispers and hush.
Let the practice infuse the marrow of your life,
So that in each moment, the sacred is rife.

title: Journey Inward: Embracing Stillness for Boundless Beauty
body:
In the quiet of morning,
when the world is yet to stir,
we find the ancient doorway,
the entry to our inner world.

Instructions come like whispered winds,
guiding us to sit, to breathe,
to hold the heart in gentle hands,
and listen to the soul beneath.

But knowledge, like a distant star,
cannot warm the waiting earth,
until the seed is sown with care,
and practice gives its purpose birth.

Each session, a sacred meeting,
a promise made with tender grace,
to journey inward, deeply seeing,
the contours of our hidden space.

We set intentions, like a compass,
to navigate the still, dark sea,
to calm the mind, to seek compassion,
to be the change we wish to see.

In the act of daily tending,
the seed begins to sprout and grow,
in patience, in the silent mending,
of all we thought we’d never know.

Through practice, we become the garden,
the fertile ground, the gentle rain,
each breath a step, each thought a pardon,
as peace flows gently through our veins.

So let us sit in morning’s hush,
with open hearts and willing hands,
to turn instructions into practice,
and weave our dreams from stillness’ strands.

For in the quiet of our being,
beneath the noise, beyond the strife,
we find the essence, softly singing,
the boundless beauty of our life.

Will you embrace this journey inward,
to see what wonders lie in wait?
In each breath, a chance for wonder,
in each moment, a path to grace.

Find more of my poems at https://www.deepermindfulness.org

title: Grounding in the Body - Per Norrgren
body:
In the quiet breath of dawn,
where the first light kisses the earth,
we find our way back to ourselves,
a journey of stillness, a path of birth.

Feet planted firm on sacred ground,
the pulse of life beneath our soles,
in this tender touch, a truth is found,
a whisper of the world’s ancient scrolls.

Here, within the temple of our flesh,
each heartbeat a gentle reminder,
that in the rush of life’s fleeting mesh,
grounding brings us moments kinder.

Feel the breath, a steady tide,
the rise and fall of life’s embrace,
in this rhythm, let the mind abide,
finding peace within each space.

The body, a vessel, a sacred place,
holding stories of joy and strife,
in its quiet wisdom, we find grace,
a deeper, richer sense of life.

Amidst the clamor of the world’s demand,
pause and breathe, feel the earth’s kiss,
grounded here, in this place we stand,
we touch the depths of inner bliss.

Each sensation, a sacred song,
sung by the flesh, the bones, the heart,
in the harmony where we belong,
our true selves, a work of art.

So let us walk with mindful feet,
upon the earth, in gentle care,
grounded in the body, life complete,
with love and presence, everywhere.

For in this grounding, we become whole,
each moment a tender caress,
in the dance of life, we find our role,
connected, loved, we are blessed.

title: The Path of Lift and Nourishment – Per Norrgren
body:
In the quiet dawn of my days, I reflect,
on the myriad paths I’ve tread, the souls I’ve met.
Each step, each word, a note in the grand symphony,
of life’s intricate melody, of moments shared, deeply.

The Threads of Connection

In the embrace of friendships, in conversations deep,
I found a wellspring, a place where spirits leap.
The touch of another’s soul, the shared laughter, the tears,
these threads of connection have woven through my years.

In the gathering of hearts, in circles of trust,
there lies a sacred alchemy, in which we must
immerse ourselves fully, without a hint of reserve,
to feel the pulse of life, to truly observe.

The Glow of Achievement

In the quiet pursuit of dreams, I’ve known the thrill,
of achievements won, by strength of heart and will.
Each milestone a testament, to persistence and grace,
a reminder that in effort, we find our place.

The moments of triumph, the goals reached with care,
each one a beacon, dispelling the despair.
For in these achievements, small and grand,
lies the proof of potential, the touch of a guiding hand.

The Nourishment of Creation

In the act of creation, in poetry and prose,
I found a nourishment that endlessly flows.
From the heart to the page, through ink and thought,
I’ve woven my experiences, the lessons life taught.

The crafting of verses, the shaping of a tale,
each one a vessel, a spirit set to sail.
Through words, I’ve explored the landscapes within,
and shared the journeys, of where I’ve been.

Opening to New Horizons

As I stand at the threshold of what’s yet to come,
I open my heart, to the rhythm, to the drum.
For there are still many paths, yet to be trod,
many connections to make, many dreams to prod.

In teaching and learning, in the simple acts of care,
in the silent meditations, in the open air,
I find new avenues, to lift and to nourish,
to live a life full, to continue to flourish.

For the essence of living, in all that we do,
is found in the moments, both many and few.
In connection, achievement, creation’s sweet song,
we discover the places, where our spirits belong.

See more poems in the App www.deepermindfulness.org

title: The Art of Control and Acceptance - Per Norrgren
body:
In the stillness of the morning dawn,
Where silence greets the waking earth,
A truth profound, in quiet drawn,
Reveals the nature of our worth.

To grasp the threads we weave each day,
And guide them with a mindful hand,
Yet let the universe, in play,
Unfold the parts we cannot command.

There is a realm within our reach,
Where effort shapes our destiny,
Yet beyond that, life’s lessons teach,
To bow with grace, to simply be.

The world, a mirror of our mind,
Reflects the ebb and flow of time,
A dance of joy and sorrow twined,
In harmony, a sacred rhyme.

So, here we stand, with hearts serene,
To nurture what we can control,
And trust the cosmic, vast unseen,
With peaceful breath, release our hold.

In this, the art of life is known,
A balance, gentle and complete,
To cherish what is ours to own,
And calmly lay the rest at fate’s feet.

For in the wisdom of this way,
We find the peace that soothes all strife,
To live in presence, day by day,
Embracing fully, this wondrous life.

title: Business – Per Norrgren
body:
In realms of business and the wider world,
Where chaos unfurls and plans are twirled,
A practice fundamental, often unsung,
Is grounding, where our best is sprung.

In high-stakes rooms, where deals are made,
And every move can cast a shade,
Staying grounded, a vital art,
Keeps us present, minds and hearts.

Focus sharpens, distractions cease,
In grounding, we find inner peace.
Resilience grows, a sturdy base,
We navigate with calm and grace.

Not just for boardrooms, this truth holds sway,
In daily life, it lights our way.
From morning dawn to evening rest,
Grounding helps us give our best.

In moments quiet, or times of strain,
When pressure mounts, or skies show rain,
A breath, a pause, to feel the ground,
In that stillness, strength is found.

It roots us firm, in storms or sun,
Reminds us all, we’re part of one.
In business ventures, or global stride,
Grounding lets our spirit guide.

So let us heed this ancient call,
To ground ourselves, lest we fall.
For in this practice, pure and true,
We find the best of what we do.

More poems in the App. https://www.deepermindfulness.net

title: Embracing the Wander - Per Norrgren
body:
In the quiet heart of stillness,
Where the mind begins to roam,
A gentle pause in mindfulness,
Turns this wandering into home.

Ah, thoughts of planning, memories dear,
A dance of mind, so wild and free,
With kindness let us draw them near,
Embrace their presence tenderly.

Gratitude for this busy mind,
Its tireless work, its endless care,
In every thought, a treasure find,
A wonder hidden everywhere.

Marvel at its ceaseless drive,
To solve, to guard, to understand,
In its quest, it keeps us alive,
A faithful guide, a helping hand.

When darkness casts its heavy veil,
And thoughts become a stormy sea,
Return to breath, let anchors sail,
Find peace in simple constancy.

In this dance of thought and calm,
A lesson deep, a wisdom true,
The mind, with all its gentle charm,
Is always doing the best it can do.

So, hold it close with tender grace,
Each thought a child, each memory dear,
In mindfulness, find sacred space,
For love and peace to reappear.

With every pause, a chance to see,
The beauty in our fleeting thoughts,
A moment of serenity,
In every lesson, wisdom sought.

Let kindness be our guiding star,
With gratitude, our hearts we fill,
In wonder, find who we are,
And in the pause, be still, be still.

title: Trust – Per Norrgren
body:
In the quiet moments of our shared breath,
Where trust is born and nurtured with care,
Our hearts and minds must align in truth,
To build a bridge, steadfast and fair.

Beneath the spoken words we share,
Lies a language pure, unseen, yet known,
Embodiment of our deepest self,
In gestures, tone, and presence shown.

With grounded heart, let intentions rise,
To meet the gaze of another’s eyes,
For in this dance of silent exchange,
True connection and trust shall thrive.

Embrace the feelings, name them clear,
With mindful breath, dispel the fear,
For every emotion, a path to grace,
In the open, honest space.

Our bodies speak a language old,
In postures open, stories told,
Relaxed and calm, with hands in sight,
We weave trust’s fabric, light and bright.

In moments of discord, find the way,
To ground the self, to calmly sway,
For in the stillness of mindful being,
Lies the essence of true seeing.

Through mindful practice, habits form,
To weather life’s relentless storm,
Embodiment of trust, we shall impart,
From soul to soul, from heart to heart.

Thus, in every word and deed,
Let trust and mindfulness be the seed,
That blossoms into bonds profound,
In the sacred circle, where peace is found.

title: Embracing Uncertainty - Per Norrgren
body:
In the quiet stillness of the heart,
Where the mind’s turmoil seeks to depart,
There lies a path, both gentle and true,
To release the uncertainties that ensue.

With each breath, we find our way,
Through the clouds of doubt, to a brighter day.
The mind, a vessel vast and deep,
Holds secrets of peace, in silence they sleep.

Uncertainty, a shadow, fleeting and thin,
Loses its grip when we turn within.
In the present moment, we gently reside,
Letting go of the fear that once did guide.

Through mindful practice, we start to see,
The boundless potential of simply to be.
The past and future, mere illusions in flight,
Dissolve in the presence of the inner light.

Awake, dear soul, to the wisdom you hold,
In the depths of your being, a story unfolds.
Of courage and clarity, of love and grace,
An endless horizon, an infinite space.

With each mindful breath, let your spirit soar,
Embrace the unknown, explore even more.
For in uncertainty, life’s true essence we find,
A dance of the heart, a freeing of the mind.

Let go of the struggle, the need to control,
Surrender to the flow, make your spirit whole.
In the embrace of now, with a heart open wide,
Discover the peace that within does reside.

So, walk with me, on this path so serene,
Through valleys of stillness, where the soul feels seen.
Together we’ll journey, with courage and care,
Releasing uncertainties, breathing the pure air.

In the vastness of being, we find our release,
From the chains of doubt, to a place of peace.
For the mind, when open, is a boundless sea,
Navigating life’s mysteries, with serene clarity.

With compassion and presence, our practice unfolds,
In the heart’s quiet whispers, the true story is told.
Of a mind unburdened, of a soul set free,
In the embrace of uncertainty, we simply be.

title: Poem: Whisper of Self-Compassion
body:
Self-compassion Introduction

In the practice of mindfulness and self-compassion, acknowledging small wins is a powerful way to foster personal growth. This poem, “Whisper of Compassion,” encapsulates the essence of self-compassion, daily achievements, and the gentle strength that comes from acts of kindness. Join me, Per Norgren, in exploring the transformative power of compassion.

Read more on the Blog

Poem: Whisper of Self-Compassion - Per Norrgren

I sit in the quiet hush of evening,
when the world sighs into stillness,
I hear a gentle whisper,
an invitation to remember.

The smallest triumphs, often hidden,
like the first light of dawn,
soft, yet persistent,
illuminating the heart’s journey.

A kind word to a stranger,
a smile shared in passing,
a task completed with care,
each a thread in a day of life.

Close your eyes and breathe,
let the day’s moments unfold,
see yourself in the dance of living,
feel the warmth of your own embrace.

“I am proud of my small wins,”
you whisper to the night,
“I am capable, I am growing,
in the garden of my heart.”

Place your hand upon your chest,
feel the rhythm of your existence,
each beat a testament to presence,
each breath a gift to be cherished.

In the story of your becoming,
compassion writes its lines,
a narrative of gentle strength,
woven with acts of kindness.

And so you walk this path,
guided by a light within,
each small win a stepping stone,
leading you home, to your heart.

Embrace this journey, tender soul,
for in the mirror of your deeds,
you’ll find the reflection of love,
the essence of who you truly are.

Let compassion be your guide,
in every moment, great or small,
for in the acknowledgment of self,
you’ll touch the hearts of all.

Conclusion:

Embracing small wins and practicing self-compassion are fundamental to personal growth and mindfulness. By reflecting on daily achievements, we cultivate a deeper sense of self-worth and kindness. Let this poem be a reminder of the gentle strength that lies within each of us, guiding us towards a compassionate and fulfilling life.

Learn more about the App, Courses and Practices: https://www.deepermindfulness.net

title: Embracing Mistakes with Kindness
body:
In the silence of our hearts,
we find the tender embrace
of every misstep, every falter.

Mistakes, like gentle whispers,
speak of our humanness,
the sacred soil from which we grow.

In the quiet corners of the mind,
we close our eyes,
revisiting the echoes of regret,
the sharp edges of frustration.

There, we meet ourselves anew,
not with the harsh voice of judgment,
but with the softness of a friend.

“It’s okay,” we whisper,
to the child within,
to the dreamer who stumbled.

For in each fall, there is a lesson,
in each misstep, a hidden grace,
waiting to be discovered.

Compassionate words flow,
like a river of forgiveness,
washing away the heaviness,
carrying us forward.

We learn to forgive,
not just the error,
but the self that dared to try.

And in this act of mercy,
we find a strength unyielding,
a courage to rise again,
to walk with renewed purpose.

So let us embrace our flaws,
with the kindness of a sunrise,
illuminating the path ahead,
each step a testament to our growth.

For in the heart of every mistake,
there lies a promise,
a beacon of light,
guiding us towards the horizon of our becoming.

-Per Norrgren

title: A Whisper of Gratitude
body:
A Whisper of Gratitude

Poem by Per Norrgren

In the quiet of dawn, a whisper we find,
A gentle reminder, a soothing touch for the mind.
In each simple act, in each humble deed,
There lies a quiet joy, a soul’s true need.

Thank you, dear self, for the morning light,
For rising with hope, embracing the fight.
In each step you take, in each breath you draw,
There is strength, there is grace, a universal law.

Thank you, dear self, for the food on your plate,
For choosing the path of love over hate.
In each meal you prepare, with hands that care,
There is a spirit of giving, a blessing to share.

Thank you, dear self, for the moments of rest,
For honouring your limits, for doing your best.
In the stillness of night, in the shadows that creep,
There is peace in your heart, a promise to keep.

Thank you, dear self, for the battles you face,
For standing with courage, for moving with grace.
In each challenge you meet, in each tear you cry,
There is growth, there is wisdom, a reason to try.

Thank you, dear self, for the laughter and tears,
For holding your dreams, despite all your fears.
In each smile you wear, in each sorrow you bear,
There is beauty, there is truth, a love so rare.

In the dance of the world, in the song of the soul,
Gratitude whispers, making us whole.
For in the heart of kindness, in the embrace of care,
We find our true selves, always aware.

So, thank you, dear self, for being so kind,
For nurturing the spirit, for freeing the mind.
In each moment of gratitude, in each gentle sigh,
There is a beacon of light, a reason to fly.

title: Poem Your Inner Light: Self-Care
body:
Wellbeing, Self-Care and Personal Growth

– Per Norrgren

There is a quiet light that lives inside you,
a steady flame unseen by hurried eyes,
yet it burns with a truth
no storm can extinguish.

In the mirror of morning, you glimpse it—
a spark of something more,
more than the self you’ve known,
more than the name you wear like a well-worn coat,
something wild,
something tender, something utterly your own.

In the hush of evening, it waits for you,
a whisper in the wind, a gentle nudge from within,
saying, Here you are.
Here you’ve always been.

This light is not for others to see,
though it colours the world with every step you take.
It is the song you have always sung,
in the silence of your heart,
in the quiet of your dreams.

There is a strength in you that bends,
but does not break,
a resilience born from a thousand dawns,
from the simple act of being yourself,
again, and again.

So stand,
not as a mountain,
but as a river— flowing, shaping,
finding your way through the rocks and the trees,
and in every curve,
celebrating the journey that is yours alone.

For in this quiet light,
you are whole, you are enough,
and the world is brighter for the gift of your presence,
for the gift of your unique,
unrepeatable soul.

title: Poem - The Quiet Line
body:
- by Per Norrgren

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses


This poem, central to wellbeing and self-car, reflects a gentle yet firm tone, exploring the theme of boundaries with a reverence for nature and a deep sense of introspection.

In the garden of morning,
where the dew settles like whispers,
I find my edges, soft yet firm,
as the earth meets the sky.

A robin calls from the oak,
reminding me of the gentle art of saying no,
a boundary as natural as the river’s course,
winding, deliberate,
through the patient land.

Here, in the stillness,
I build my walls with care,
not to keep out the world,
but to hold close what is tender within me,
a small sanctuary of peace,
where the heart can rest,
unfettered by the pull of others’ desires.

I learn from the wild geese,
who fly together, yet apart,
each knowing its place in the sky,
each honouring the space that keeps them aloft.

And so, I too, shall keep my distance,
not from love,
but from the weight of it,
when it presses too hard against the boundaries
I have drawn in the sand.

For in these lines,
I find my freedom,
and in this freedom,
I find myself,
whole, unbroken,
a quiet flame burning brightly in the dusk.

title: Poem - Naming the Storm
body:
- by Per Norrgren

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

In the quiet breath before the storm,
I stand with a heart full of whispers,
The tempest gathers at the edges of thought,
But I, in this fragile moment,
Reach out to the clouds within,
And name them.

Fear, like a shadowed raven,
Flies close to my skin,
Its wings brushing against the delicate bones
Of my resolve.
But when I speak its name,
The feathers fall like autumn leaves,
And the sky, once choked with thunder,
Clears.

Anger, a flame that leaps and curls,
Threatening to consume the forest of my calm,
Burns less brightly when I call it forth,
A fire known is a fire tamed,
The blaze dwindles to embers,
And I, the quiet keeper of its name,
Am no longer its fuel.

In the naming, there is a surrender,
Not of power, but of the need to control,
For what is named is understood,
And what is understood
Can be held with tender hands,
No longer a beast in the night,
But a creature of the day,
Tamed by the simple act of being seen.

Here, in the aftermath of words,
I walk through the fields of my mind,
Where emotions once raged,
Now soft with the bloom of peace.
Each one, a name whispered to the wind,
A storm passed, a calm found,
And I, the namer of my own heart,
Am free.

On the edge of the world where the salt meets the sky,
Wells next the Sea, where the seabirds cry,
I find myself in quiet, drawn by the pull
Of something ancient, something full.

The tides ebb softly, but within, they rise,
Whispers of truth beneath the still skies.
In the hush of these moments, I begin to see—
Not the world as it is, but the world in me.

Silent, we gather, a circle of souls,
Each breath a step towards making us whole.
Nature unfolds, patient and true,
Reflecting a mirror for me and for you.

We stand as one, but inside, we part—
Each on a journey, deep in the heart.
Through trees and wind, through sky and sea,
We discover the boundless, the quiet “me.”

Together we are, yet alone in our quest,
Finding stillness, and in stillness, rest.
The waves speak softly of all that’s been,
Of all we are, and all we’ve seen.

And when the sun sets on our final day,
It carries a message far and away—
That in silence, love’s voice can be heard,
In the quiet of self, without a word.

I sat with my sorrow,

in the soft gathering of yourself
when the day is done,
there is a strength that is yours,
unchanging and true,
as steady as the roots

invisible but present,

Here, in the warmth of your heart’s embrace,
You are home, you are safe, in your own sacred space.

Threads of Belonging

In the hum of the city, the quiet heart beats,
Where streets whisper stories, and every soul meets.
We walk, unseen, yet woven as one,
Beneath the vast sky, under moon, under sun.

Your breath is a thread, soft, strong, and true,
Binding you here to the whole, to the new.
The breeze that brushes, the bird that sings,
Each carries a note of the connection it brings.

See the hand of the world reaching to you,
Through pavement and petals, in grey and in blue.
Feel the warmth of a stranger’s unseen care,
A silent embrace in the open air.

We are more than our shadows, our joys, and our strife,
We’re the pulse of the world, the rhythm of life.
So pause, and feel it, the love that surrounds,
The quiet belonging in small, sacred sounds.

You’re here, and it’s enough, no need to be more,
You’re the shore meeting waves, the heart at the core.
Together we rise, unseen yet profound,
In the fabric of all, where love is found.

title: Grounding in Hope
body:
Grounding in Hope

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

Rest your soul, let the earth hold tight,
Feel its strength in the morning light.
A silent promise, steady and true,
The ground beneath is here for you.

Within your chest, a warmth begins,
A gentle light that softly spins.
It whispers calm, it whispers care,
A love unbroken, always there.

No need to run, no need to race,
For hope resides in this quiet place.
A seed of trust, so small, so still,
It grows within, a mighty will.

The storms may rise, the shadows creep,
Yet hope endures, steadfast and deep.
In every breath, in every sigh,
A tender strength that lifts you high.

So rest, my child, and find your peace,
In love’s embrace, let striving cease.
For where the heart finds warmth and grace,
Hope will bloom in its sacred space.

title: Poem - The Quiet Knowing
body:
The Quiet Knowing

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

In the stillness, I find myself—
not as the world demands I be,
but as the soft breath of my own becoming.
Here, I am neither past nor future,
only the tender weight of now.

The pond reflects what I cannot yet say,
its surface a quiet witness to my truths.
The ripples whisper: This is you,
not the striving, nor the shadow,
but the steady presence beneath it all.

In the hush of togetherness,
I feel the current of being—
not yours, not mine, but ours,
woven in the quiet rhythm
that beats between hearts, between lives.

And as I sit, the mind softens,
the heart opens,
the endless doing dissolves
into the gentle ease of being.

Here, I am whole,
not because I am finished,
but because I am here,
alive in the pulse of what is,
connected to the vast stillness,
and at last,
at home.

title: Poem - The First Step

Poem - The First Step

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

It begins here,
in the quiet hum of now,
where the world waits—not for greatness,
but for the smallest movement of your heart,
the barest shift of your foot
toward what calls.

The future does not arrive
in sweeping gestures
or bold proclamations.
It sneaks in
through the doorway of this moment,
the gentle act of beginning,
the soft courage of leaning forward.

You are not asked to conquer mountains,
only to take the first step
on the winding road
that feels like home.

The birds do not plan their flight;
they lift their wings.
The stream does not question its journey;
it flows.
And you—
you are built of the same quiet power,
the same whispered knowing
that calls the seed to root,
the sun to rise,
the breath to carry on.

So walk.
Not for the end,
but for the beauty of motion itself.
For the way hope unfolds
when action meets intention,
and the way the world changes
when you do.

title: Poem - From Fear To Curiosity
body:
Poem - From Fear To Curiosity

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

When shadows fall and fear takes hold,
A trembling heart, a story untold.
Pause, dear one, and softly say,
“I see you here; it’s okay to stay.”

In the quiet space, breathe deep and true,
Hold your fear as the sky holds dew.
No need to banish, no need to fight,
For even fear can birth new light.

What if this weight, so heavy, so near,
Is not a foe but a guide sincere?
An open hand, a whispered plea,
“Come closer now, explore with me.”

Transform the shadow, let it bloom,
A curious spark in the darkest room.
Ask the question, take one small stride,
Feel the fear shift to wonder inside.

Each step you take, no matter how small,
Is a gentle act of hope for all.
A bridge is built where a chasm lay,
Fear melts to curiosity’s ray.

So walk this path, let courage unfold,
The journey’s yours, let the story be told.
For within each moment, raw and true,
Lies the adventure waiting for you.

title: Poem - The Thread of Purpose
body:
The Thread of Pupose

Try Deeper Mindfulness App
FREE Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

In the stillness of this moment,
as the day stretches its golden arms wide,
I feel the quiet hum of being,
the weightless thread that pulls me home.

It begins deep within—
a whisper, not a roar,
soft as the rustle of leaves,
steady as the tides meeting the shore.

This is the togetherness of being,
the unspoken bond we all carry,
woven in the fabric of breath and gaze,
in the silent nod of recognition.

I reach into myself,
not to change,
but to see—
to trace the shape of my belonging,
the contours of my true nature.

What I find is not grand or loud,
but tender, like the first bloom of spring,
a purpose stitched into the marrow
of this fleeting, wondrous life.

It is here, now,
in the ripple of shared laughter,
in the hand held, the word offered,
in the earth beneath bare feet.

And in this stillness,
the world opens, wide and vast,
not to show me my place within it,
but to remind me
I am it—
inseparable, whole, infinite.

So I walk this path,
not searching,
but becoming.
With every step, a quiet knowing:
the purpose I seek
has always been
in the pulse of my heart,
the rhythm of this life.

title: Poem - A Stillness Unfolding

A Stillness Unfolding

Join the Deeper Mindfulness Community
FREE LIVE and RECORDED Mindfulness Courses

-by Per Norrgren

Sit here, just here,
where the breath leans into the body,
where the morning light folds itself into your skin,
where silence asks for presence.

You are not the frown,
nor the storm behind your brow.
You are the watcher,
the one who listens,
to the tiny gestures of your body.

Feel the lift of breath,
the way your lips soften into kindness,
Feel your jaw letting go,
as if the whole world no longer needs,
to be held in your teeth.

You were never separate from this moment,
never apart from the river of being,
each smile, each exhale,
each quiet unraveling of what was clenched.

A gift, to know yourself this way—
to witness the shifting tides of feeling,
to stand at the edge of emotions,
and choose to return to stillness.

In this moment the great togetherness of being—
the knowing that you were never alone,
that you belong to the breath and the body,
to the vast and tender space of now.

title: Poem - The breath of my life
body:

The Breach Of My Life

- by Per Norrgren

I wake to the hush of morning,
the sky still quiet, the world just beginning—
and my breath, soft as a wave returning to shore,
is the first thing I notice.

I follow it as it rises,
a wind through hollow reeds,
a river smoothing the stones of my ribs,
a bird lifting into an unmarked sky.

Oh, what a wonder, this breath,
this gentle, tireless companion,
walking with me through sorrow,
dancing with me in joy,
whispering—stay, stay, stay.

And when the world leans too close,
when the weight of the days gathers in my chest,
I turn again to the rhythm that never leaves me,
the tide that does not falter.

It is not the noise that saves me,
but the quiet between—
a breath held, then given,
as if the whole earth were exhaling with me.

Come, sit with me.
Feel the wind through your ribs,
the steady tide beneath your hand,
the way breath carries you home.

The morning inside me

I did not wake
to the sound of clocks,
but to something older—
a presence stirring
beneath the skin of thought,
beneath the known world.

The morning did not arrive
through the window,
but through the chest,
a slow unfolding
of breath,
as if light had remembered
where I live.

I rose not from sleep,
but from forgetting—
and found again
the quiet architecture
of being,
the soft floor
beneath all striving.

There,
in the hush between
the last dream
and the first demand,
I met myself again—
not the self that performs,
not the self that proves,
but the one that listens.

And what a miracle
that stillness speaks.
What a mercy
that silence waits.
What a home
to return to.

How to Meet the World

- Per Norrgren

Start with the morning—
its quiet astonishment
that you are here
again.

Feel the breath
enter the soft house
of the body,
and leave gently,
like a guest
that knows the way.

Then—
before the list,
before the news,
before the mirror asks
too many questions—
go outside.

Let the wind touch your face
like it remembers you.
Let the birds remind you
how joy sounds
when it doesn’t explain itself.

And smile—
not the polished kind,
not the one worn for company—
but the slow,
unfolding curve
that rises
when the heart recognises
its own aliveness.

Meet the world
as if it might forgive itself today.
As if you could too.
As if this—this breath, this light,
this wildly ordinary moment—
was already enough.

The Companion

 - by Per Norrgren  (Click here to listen to the poem)

I have walked so far—
through nettled fields and mornings glazed
with frost and longing.
I have leaned my ear to the wind,
waiting for some answer
that never came
from the hills or the river.

But always the grasses waved.
Always the robins returned.
Always the moon was kind.

And one day, in the stillness
between a breath and a step,
I noticed:
the hush in my chest was not loneliness,
but listening.

All this time—
it was me, walking beside me.
Me, making the tea.
Me, watching the light
fold gently through the trees.

Oh, what a fierce tenderness to realise:
I am not waiting to be chosen.
I was never unchosen.
I am the one I’ve been travelling with,
through sunburn and sorrow,
through laughter I thought would never return.

And now,
with the earth soft beneath my feet,
I say to the sky,
and to the smallest cricket singing in the hedge—

I am here.
And I will not leave myself again.

Stillness at the End

You were never loud about your goodness—
you simply moved through the days
with the steady hands of someone
who had made peace with work,
with silence,
with the weight of things not spoken.

You taught me
how to listen by how you listened,
how to stay by how you stayed—
not clinging, not demanding,
just there.
Like the shape of a harbour
welcomes the tide.

You weren’t a man of ceremony,
but you made the ordinary sacred—
a chair by the window,
the folding of a shirt,
a look that said more than words
would dare to.

And in the end,
there was no thunder,
no last performance.
Just breath that softened into air,
hands that let go without struggle,
and your cheek, still warm
as the morning rose.

If this was goodbye,
then let it be known:
you were
a man who loved well,
and was well loved.

And I—
who once reached up for your hand,
now carry your stillness in mine.

The Feel of Things

I went to the woods not to walk,
but to listen for what moves beneath the fern,
to feel the hush between wind and wing.
 
The moss, when touched, told me
everything has its own soft response—
the stone, a cool indifference;
the larkspur, a gentle yes.
 
There, I learned the body keeps its own conversation.
A flutter behind the ribs
at the sound of water returning to its course.
A tightening at the call of the hawk.
The way the skin knows before the mind.
 
I did not need answers.
Only to notice.
Only to name the invisible pull—
the leaning toward or away.
 
Even in silence, something in me was always choosing:
this joy, let it stay.
this ache, not now.
this emptiness—perhaps, I will fill it with sky.
 
But then I saw it—
how each feeling, each flicker,
was just a cloud skimming the lake’s surface,
never asking to be caught or pushed away.
 
I sat on the damp ground,
hands open in the lap of myself,
and finally said:
“Let it all be.”
 
And in that moment,
I became the pond that welcomed every ripple.
The fox that watched but did not chase.
The tree that bent but did not break.
 
Oh, the tenderness of this world,
when you meet it with soft eyes—
not to fix, not to hold—
but to feel, and let go,
and feel again.

When the Field Asks Nothing

One day,
in the small hour between the blackbird’s call
and the sun’s slow unbuttoning of the mist,
I walked to the edge of the field—
where sorrow had been keeping its quiet tent
just beneath the sedge.

There, the wind did not ask
if I was brave,
nor did the nettle
apologise for its sting.

A hare startled from the tall grass
as if to say:
run if you must—
but know the stillness
was here all along.

I sat.
Not in triumph. Not in grief.
Just the way a stone sits
in the river’s wide patience.

The ache in my chest
was not a curse
but weather.

And the breath?
It softened the belly,
like rain softens old clay
until it becomes a vessel again.

A crow circled, watching,
and the sky,
spacious as mercy,
held it all.

That was the day I stopped demanding
that difficulty leave.
Instead, I said:
You may sit here, too,
if you can be quiet.

And it did.
And we watched the light
walk slowly over the hills.

What the Mind Meant to Say

I came late to the garden—
the wind had already shaken the birch leaves down,
and the grasses bowed their golden heads
as if remembering something sorrowful
and kind.

The stone by the path was warm still,
and I sat,
not to solve anything,
not to ask for clarity,
but simply to be a witness
to the way the world goes on
no matter how heavy my thoughts.

A sparrow flung its song into the air
as if joy were weightless
and belonging was not a prize to be earned
but a birthright
you could return to
with every breath.

The mind,
with its clever reels and riddles,
had meant to interrupt.
But today it softened—
and I saw what it had been trying to say all along:
I am not your enemy.
I am only trying to keep you safe.

Then silence opened like a gate,
and I stepped through
with nothing in my hands
but the feel of the earth beneath me,
and a quiet promise
to remember the light.

When the storm is inside us

When the storm is not in the sky
but coiled behind your ribs,
spinning the sea of your stomach—
you must answer it not with silence,
but with movement.

Press your feet into the dirt
the way the heron presses down
before lifting herself from the reed-bed.
Swing your arms like branches do
when wind pulls its thousand stories
through the trees.

Lift your body—slowly—
like the tide lifting driftwood,
then let it fall again,
a soft surrender.
Rock your spine like the dunes
shift under the moon.

And in the doing,
you will remember
that the body is older than thought—
and wiser.

And that even the wildest wind
knows how to settle,
when the earth stands steady beneath it.

When the tide comes home

There is a place beyond the dunes
where the wind leans in
only to listen.

You walk there —
not to find anything,
but to let the sand remember your feet.

A heron lifts,
slow as forgiveness,
from the silver mouth of the creek.
Its wings do not ask the air for permission.

Here, the salt grass bends to you,
the sun lays its warm hand
across your shoulders,
and the restless water says,
It was always you.

You stand in the wide, bare morning
and notice how the world holds you —
not as a prize,
not as a burden,
but as a stone belongs to the river,
a cloud belongs to the blue.

And in that soft, unarguable belonging,
you turn inward,
meet the one you have been carrying all your life,
and say — at last —
Yes.

The joy of finding strength within

I did not know the granite was in me,
until the wind leaned hard against my chest
and I did not topple.

I thought myself a reed,
all sway and tremble,
but somewhere beneath the quiet soil of my ribs
a root had gone down deep,
seeking water older than rain.

The hawk circles,
the river keeps moving —
all the while a steady rhythm grows inside,
a drumbeat older than fear,
you could call it the heart,
or the earth remembering itself through me.

What a joy,
to stand among the pines
and realise they are not only beside me,
but within me —
their tall patience,
their dark green certainty
woven into my blood.

Strength is not thunder
or a shout across the valley.
It is the way the oak leans into winter,
the way the fox steps lightly across the frost,
the way I rise each morning
and find myself still here,
a little more unshaken,
a little more whole.

And I think —
perhaps this is what joy means:
not a fleeting spark,
but the slow, golden knowing
that what holds the mountain upright
also holds me.

Rooted Strength

Beneath the restless grasses,
the roots go on weaving,
knitting a thousand filaments into the dark earth,
holding what the storms cannot take.

I think of the trees—
how they do not tremble with every passing wind,
but rise steady,
their trunks carrying both gravity and grace.
Even the smallest sapling
leans into the air as if it knows
the secret of endurance.

And I remember
that my own body is not so different:
bones are my stones,
muscles the braided vines,
breath the river that keeps it all alive.

So when the day wavers,
when the voices of doubt climb like ivy
toward the fragile places,
I press my feet into the soil,
curl my toes into the hum of the ground,
and lift my spine—
a green shoot among countless others,
quietly declaring,
I will not fall.

Strength, I learn,
is not the shout of conquest
but the steady pulse of belonging:
to the earth,
to the breath,
to the quiet hand resting on my heart,
saying only—
stay.

The bird that dares the morning

At first, the world is still,
a hush spread over the meadow,
dew clinging like a thousand tiny silences.
 
And then —
a single bird lifts its throat to the air,
a thread of sound unwinding into the dawn.
 
It does not ask
whether the forest will answer,
whether the sky will bend closer
to catch its fragile note.
 
It sings because it must,
because the body holds music
the way rivers hold their hidden stones.
 
So, too, in you —
the voice waiting behind the ribs,
the truth pressing gently at the lips.
 
Speak it.
Not for applause, not for safety,
but because the morning is yours to meet,
and the air is wide enough
to carry everything you are.

Horizon after the storm

The sky has torn itself open,
the storm’s last mutter fading
into the far hills.

The air is rinsed clean—
trees stand taller,
the river loosens its silver tongue.

You stand there too,
not smaller than the world,
but widened with it,
your chest a shoreline
where breath meets the sea.

How long you carried the tightness—
the small rooms of worry,
the clenched heart.
And now—see—
the horizon has no edges.

In the vast blue,
your voice could rise
like a bird
and still not fill the silence.

Here is the secret:
to open is not to be broken,
to expand is not to be lost,
but to belong—
to everything,
to yourself,
to the trembling joy
of this wide and possible world.

[fusion_builder_container type="flex" hundred_percent="no" equal_height_columns="no" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" background_position="center center" background_repeat="no-repeat" fade="no" background_parallax="none" parallax_speed="0.3" video_aspect_ratio="16:9" video_loop="yes" video_mute="yes" border_style="solid"][fusion_builder_row][fusion_builder_column type="1_1" layout="1_1" background_position="left top" border_style="solid" border_position="all" spacing="yes" background_repeat="no-repeat" margin_top="0px" margin_bottom="0px" animation_speed="0.3" animation_direction="left" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" center_content="no" last="true" hover_type="none" background_blend_mode="overlay" first="true"][fusion_text]

When the Past Came Walking

It was morning,
early light spilled like milk
across the trembling grass.
The sky, with its long, aching arms,
held no grudge.

I walked the edge of the field—
barefoot, unafraid—
where the wind remembered
what I’d tried to forget.

The past came,
not as a storm this time,
not with teeth or ruin,
but soft-footed as a deer,
pausing among the birches.

And I—
I had grown tired of running,
of casting stones into dark water,
hoping echoes could be rewritten.

I opened my chest
like the morning opens the hill,
and let it see
the bird still singing inside me.

And in that meeting—
sun through ash leaves,
breath where sorrow once nested—
a shadow lifted.

And when I turned
to face the day,
the whole field
was waiting.
Not to be explained—
just walked into.
Barefoot.
Alive.

body:

When the past knocks softly

There’s a path that begins
where the grasses lean westward,
brushed by the sighs of women who once ran,
barefoot,
from the things they could not name.

There, the wind doesn’t ask for your story.
It already knows.
It has carried the ache of ancient daughters,
the long breath of grandmothers
who learned to swallow thunder.

Still—
there are violets growing
out of the ashes of all your endings.
There is moss thick enough
to cradle the hardest question.

The past will come again,
not as a villain but a deer
stepping shyly from the trees—
its eyes wide with memory,
its ribs sharp with hunger.

You do not have to run.
You do not have to silence your heartbeat.
You do not have to give it your hands.

Just sit,
sun on your back,
and watch it watching you.

The shadows will move—
as shadows do—
but they will not devour you.
They do not own the light.

Breathe here.
Let the wind fill you with something
older than fear—
something like spring returning
through frost.

You are not broken.
You are becoming.

And still, the world leans close

The wind doesn’t ask
if you’ve been kind enough today,
or quiet enough,
or if your hands have done
anything worthy of being held.
It brushes your cheek anyway—
gently, as if you belonged.

The birch tree does not question
your reason for pausing beside her.
She simply offers her shimmering silence,
her small, trembling dance
for no one in particular.

Look how the river keeps moving,
as if it knows something about carrying on
without needing to understand.
And the hawk, looping circles overhead—
she does not land to instruct you,
but her flight might teach you
how to widen.

Somewhere, a blade of grass
is pushing through dry ground,
green with the knowledge
that everything begins again,
and again.

So go on—
feel the sun like a forgiveness
you didn’t have to earn.
Let the world lean close.
Let it speak its thousand languages
of light and leaf and echo.

Let that be enough,
for now.
Let that be your belonging.

What the light did

It was nothing—
just a single shaft of late sun
falling across the mossy fence
as I passed through
the worn wooden gate
I’d walked by a hundred times
and never really seen.

But this time,
the light landed
like a whisper I’d been waiting for,
soft and golden and utterly indifferent
to if I was ready.

A bird startled upward—
that sharp flutter of wings
a punctuation mark
on the sentence I hadn’t known I was living.

And there,

the whole sky leaned in.

My chest opened
the way a window does
in spring
when you finally trust
that the cold might be finished.

And what filled it wasn’t clarity,
or purpose,
or some tidy knowing—

just a stillness,
vast and kind,
where I remembered
what it is
to be part of the world
and not apart from it.

What the stillness teaches

Out beyond the tangled noise
of inboxes and inner negotiations,
beyond the brittle edge of holding it together —
there is a field of silver grasses,
wind-laced and unconcerned.

I went there with tired bones,
with the weight of doing strapped across my chest
like a too-tight harness.
The sky did not ask me to explain.
The trees did not comment
on my lateness to myself.

They simply kept being what they are —
steady, slow-growing,
wise in a language I had forgotten.

I sat in the salt air,
my breath unsure at first,
like a creature emerging
from the wrong kind of forest.

And slowly my spine uncurled.
The grip loosened.
Thoughts, like birds,
flew in and out of me without nesting.

Something ancient and kindly
began to hum again —
a rhythm beneath the rhythms.

The wind moved over my skin
and said nothing.
Still — I heard everything.
And when I stood hours later,
no longer braced against
the ordinary ache.

I knew this:
stillness is not a luxury.
It is a kind of medicine.
And the world —
looked gentler,
because I was.

What the distance showed me

I had tried — the way people do —
to become wise by staying where I was.
I had filled notebooks with well-intentioned words,
sat on the cushion as instructed,
Peeled back the layers with careful questions.

But the fog, gentle and stubborn, lingered.
Until one morning, without planning it, I left.
I left the buzzing lights,
the list by the kettle,
the pings and pulls of a well-meaning life —
and walked towards the water.

The wind did not ask what I hoped to find.
It simply moved. And so did I.
The tide was going out.
Gulls circled, indifferent.
Grasses bent at the root
without needing to explain their surrender.

And somewhere in all that unconcerned beauty,
my effort dissolved.
Not into despair, but into a kind of welcome.
Like the horizon itself was saying:
You do not have to wrestle insight
from every moment.
Some truths arrive only when you step away
from the centre of the storm.

I sat on the dunes.
Did nothing useful.
Let the silence breathe through me like a tide through rockweed.
And in that space — not filled with achievement,
but with air — something cleared.

Not all at once, and not forever, but enough.
Enough to see that not-knowing is not a failure.
That stillness is not the absence of work,
but the beginning of a different kind.

I rose, salt on my lips, lighter in the joints.
Not because I’d solved it,
but because I’d remembered who was asking the questions.
The world had not changed. But I had.
And that was enough for now.

What we carry

Not everything we carry
is heavy.

Some things—
a glance,
a birdsong,
the way a child once reached for your hand without looking—
tuck themselves quietly into the folds of the heart,
and stay.

You could walk for years and forget their names,
but not their shape.
Not the warmth they made.

These moments do not shout.
They do not knock.
They do not insist on being healed or solved or even remembered properly.
But they hum.
Softly.
Like roots singing in the dark.

A bowl of oranges on a sunlit table.
The breathless stillness just after snowfall.
The exact moment you knew you would say yes.

They are all still here—
not gone,
not lost,
not diminished by time—
but gathered.

The way the sea gathers light.
The way the earth gathers rain.
The way your own chest gathers breath when something finally makes sense.

So walk gently.
You are not alone.
You are accompanied by all the quiet things,
that ever made you feel most alive.

To catch the moment

It will not knock.
It will not wait.
It does not ask if you are ready
or dressed
or in the mood to be changed.

It arrives as a breath,
a flick of sunlight on stone,
the wild rasp of a crow cutting across
your carefully made plans.

You were walking somewhere.
Thinking of something.
Trying to be someone.

But the moment had other ideas.
It curled itself inside the wind
and brushed the back of your neck
like an old friend
you hadn’t thought to miss.

You paused.
And the world opened.
Not like thunder.
More like a meadow does—
slowly, with no apology
for how long it took.

And inside that opening:
your breath,
your heartbeat,
your one precious, breakable life
remembering how to belong
to something
that does not need to be fixed
or won
or earned.

You looked up,
and for no particular reason,
everything made sense.

That was the moment.
It did not save you.
It simply waited
to be noticed.

This is how the world enters you

Not with thunder.
Not with a sermon.
But with the rustle of grass you almost didn’t hear
because you were thinking about your inbox.

With the hush between birdcalls,
the exact shape of silence
in the trees.

This is how the moment asks to be noticed—
not as a lesson but as a friend
who doesn’t need fixing.

You step outside,
not looking for anything.
And there it is: light on the bark,
wind on your cheek,
the old ache in your chest softened by the scent of rain.

You don’t have to name it.
Or hold it.
Or keep it for later.

Just let it in.
Let it fill the wide cathedral of your ribs
and echo down the quiet corridors of your attention.

This is not escape.
This is return.
This is the moment reminding you that you belong
to something gentle,
and real,
and already happening.

title: Poem - The Ten Fields
body:
[fusion_builder_container type="flex" hundred_percent="no" equal_height_columns="no" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" background_position="center center" background_repeat="no-repeat" fade="no" background_parallax="none" parallax_speed="0.3" video_aspect_ratio="16:9" video_loop="yes" video_mute="yes" border_style="solid"][fusion_builder_row][fusion_builder_column type="1_1" layout="1_1" background_position="left top" border_style="solid" border_position="all" spacing="yes" background_repeat="no-repeat" margin_top="0px" margin_bottom="0px" animation_speed="0.3" animation_direction="left" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" center_content="no" last="true" hover_type="none" background_blend_mode="overlay" first="true"][fusion_text animation_direction="left" animation_speed="0.3" animation_delay="0" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" sticky_display="normal,sticky"]

The Ten Fields

Out past the noise of engines and errands,
I walked until the earth spoke plain.
Not in words, but in the pulse that steadied underfoot —
the old reassurance: you are held.
That was Safety, the first field, where moss builds its patient empire
and roots do their silent arithmetic.

Further on, the path bent toward a stand of birch.
Each tree leaned to another, their white skins touching.
That was Belonging — the way trunks, even when apart, share the wind.

A kestrel flashed overhead, a strike of purpose.
That was Agency, clean and precise,
no apology for hunger or direction.

By the river, light played with water.
Every ripple was an attempt, every glint a reward.
That was Valuation,
the river saying: effort is never wasted if it moves you toward the sea.

At the canyon’s rim, thorn and blossom lived in the same stem.
That was Boundary, the art of being both invitation and defence.

In a meadow, two deer nosed each other’s flanks, then bounded away together —
the grace of Intimacy, the knowledge that closeness requires space to run.

Later, clouds opened and rain wrote its silver handwriting on the soil.
The land drank without complaint —
that was Contribution, the joy of giving back what one has been given.

High on the ridge, hawks spiralled in quiet argument about the wind.
That was Status,
the instinct to find one’s height without forgetting the thermals that lift all wings.

Dusk came, and the world loosened its boundaries —
foxes began their patrol, a moth tested the night.
That was Exploration, the soft curiosity that outlives daylight.

And when the stars arrived, the last field opened —
Transcendence, where even fear remembers its lineage to wonder.
I stood there, breathing the old air that has seen everything and still forgives.

Sometimes you don’t need to master your feelings.
You only need to walk until each one finds its landscape,
and the body, recognising the terrain, calls it home.

When the wind knows your name

When you are full of storm,
go out where the fields have no edges.
Let the tall grasses do the talking.
They will not ask what’s wrong.
They have known worse weather.

Take your sadness to the hill—
it has held a thousand such burdens.
Stand there until your pulse
matches the wind’s long breath,
and you remember that movement
is the oldest form of forgiveness.

If you are frightened,
watch how the light enters the water,
how it never asks permission
to tremble or to shine.

If you are angry,
look at the hawk:
she spends her fury on the wing,
and when it’s done,
she circles back to silence.

There is a calm that will not come
from thought, or speech, or solving—
only from standing still long enough
to feel the small green insistence
of the world that keeps beginning.

And when you return,
your chest a little wider,
your eyes rinsed clean,
you’ll understand:
managing your emotions
was never the point.
The point was learning
to let the earth hold them with you.

title: Poem - The Field That Waits for You

[fusion_builder_container type="flex" hundred_percent="no" equal_height_columns="no" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" background_position="center center" background_repeat="no-repeat" fade="no" background_parallax="none" parallax_speed="0.3" video_aspect_ratio="16:9" video_loop="yes" video_mute="yes" border_style="solid"][fusion_builder_row][fusion_builder_column type="1_1" layout="1_1" background_position="left top" border_style="solid" border_position="all" spacing="yes" background_repeat="no-repeat" margin_top="0px" margin_bottom="0px" animation_speed="0.3" animation_direction="left" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" center_content="no" last="true" hover_type="none" background_blend_mode="overlay" first="true"][fusion_text animation_direction="left" animation_speed="0.3" animation_delay="0" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" sticky_display="normal,sticky"]

The Field That Waits for You

There is a field that waits for you —
not with banners,
not with applause —
only the hush of grass bending
to the wind that wants to be moved.
 
You have stood there before,
arms heavy as wet bark,
believing the earth indifferent.
You forgot that the wind itself
asks for your breath to join it.
 
Bend once.
Touch the ground.
The soil will answer — a low hum,
ancient and sure:
You act, therefore you belong.
 
A single step stirs ants and seeds,
and already the geometry of things
re-writes itself around you.
Even the smallest gesture
tilts the sunlight a fraction more toward life.
 
Anger too has a place here —
a red fox in the reeds,
startled, alive, refusing disappearance.
Let it run; watch it find the treeline;
that is fairness returning to its wild body.
 
Do not wait for the sky to instruct you.
Move, and the sky will shift its clouds
to make room for your motion.
 
And when you rest again,
the wind, the soil, the fox, the sunlight —
all will know:
you have remembered the oldest law —
that action is prayer,
and every honest effort
tilts the world a little toward justice.

The Warm Animal of the World

I sat beneath the leaning birch
and thought I was alone.
But the wind touched my sleeve —
and for a moment,
I remembered the language of warmth.

The earth breathed;
the small birds rearranged themselves in the hedge.
I heard, in that soft confusion,
the body of the world saying,
Stay.

The sky seemed clear
But with haze and a glow

All the way to the moon

So I placed my hand over my heart
and found a rhythm not entirely mine —
something older, shared.
Even the silence hummed with company.

I did not need to speak.
The pulse of belonging
was already answering.
I listened deeply and finally found
The warmth of the me,
so profound.

The Line That Breathes

There is a line in the field,
you cannot see it—
it hums beneath the grass,
a tremor where root meets air.

Stand there awhile.
The wind will test your stance,
the crows will shout their opinions,
the ground will steady you anyway.

You will feel the heat
that rises in your chest—
a wild animal of protection
who only ever wanted to love safely.

Breathe with it.
Let it press its head against your palm,
let it know the door is open,
but the house is yours.

Some days the heart wants to close,
to build walls of thistle and iron.
Some days it forgets
that the same hand can hold and say no.

Stay until you remember.
Until your breath becomes the boundary—
soft, sure, alive—
and the horizon bows back,
not in surrender, but in respect.

Because the field is still yours,
and you are still of the field.
Nothing lost,
only the shape of belonging found.

Enoughness

There is a hillside where the wind keeps its own counsel,
where the grasses lean and whisper not of striving
but of simply being touched by light.

Go there in your mind.
Stand in that wide, forgiving field.
Feel how the earth lifts you without asking for improvement,
how the sky recognises you without needing achievement.

Every blade of grass holds its place without trying.
Every bird sings without wondering if its song will be heard.

You, too, were made for this.
For the soft yielding of the chest,
the quiet rising of the back,
the gentle truth that what you offer does not need applause to be real.

Somewhere within you is a pulse that says simply:
Enough.
Enough for this moment,
enough for this life,
enough for the quiet dignity of being here at all.

Stand in that field a little longer.
Let the warmth gather in your hands.
Let the breath widen the cage around your heart.

And listen—
not for praise,
but for the small, certain voice that rises like morning inside your own chest:

“I count.”

Weather of the heart

Morning light drifted through the trees,
quiet as a held breath,
and I found myself thinking
of all the ways a person learns
to harden against the world.

nothing becomes tough
without a history of weather.

Beneath all that armour,

a tenderness waiting,
a warmth not forgotten,
just buried for safety.

The forest offered no judgement,
only its simple truth:
everything opens again
when the season is right,
when the cold has finally passed.

I breathe with the morning,
letting the branches sway above me,
and feel the quiet mercy
of seeing another’s weather
instead of their walls.

When the Field Finally Called My Name

For years I walked at the edges of things—the quiet person,
the one who learned to fold himself
into smaller and smaller shapes,
as if absence were a kind of safety.

I knew the feel of vanishing:
the chest gone soft,
the voice retreating,
the earth beneath my feet
holding me without my knowing it.

There was a season when the world grew large around me
and I grew small inside it,
like a stone dropped into tall grass—still present,
but unseen even by myself.

But one morning,
in a wind that carried the scent of rain,
I felt something shift— a subtle widening beneath my ribs,
a lifting in the spine,
a whisper from the ground saying,
You belong, too.

I stood there as light came through the trees
in thin, forgiving lines,
and realised the forest
had never once asked me
to shrink.

And in that small re-inhabiting,
I felt the world turn toward me—
not because I demanded it,
but because I had finally
turned toward myself.

Now, when the wind moves the grass,
I remember the long years of hiding,
and the moment the field
finally called my name.

And I stepped forward—
no longer the outline of a man,
but the whole of one.

title: Poem - The way the light found me

The way the light found me

For a long time I lived like a shadow
moving along the edges of things—
a thin presence,
barely disturbing the dust on the path.

Some mornings I would stand in the doorway
and watch the world go about its business:
wind in the birches,
the quiet concentration of a river rounding a stone,
the fields opening themselves to weather and time.

I felt small beside them,
as if the world knew something about belonging
that I had forgotten.

But one day
—no different from the rest—
I noticed the light falling through the branches,
the way it touched the folded places in the grass
and made them rise.

Something in me leaned toward that brightness,
just a little,
the way a stem tilts before anyone can see it move.

And in that small leaning I sensed the earth
calling my weight back to it,
the ribs widening as if they remembered a long-lost instruction,
the breath returning with its soft, patient hands.

Since then I have walked more slowly,
letting the world touch me as it wishes—
a warm stone in the pocket,
the steady lift of birds at dawn,
the river speaking in its clear, unfinished sentences.

And sometimes,
in the open field where the wind gathers,
I feel myself fully here— not larger,
simply present— as if nothing in me needs to hide from the day.

Just the quiet fact of being alive,
and the light finding me exactly as I am.

After the long Winter

There was a time when I moved through the world
like a tree in deep winter—
standing, yes,
but unnoticed,
the branches holding their stories close to the bark,
the sky passing over me without a pause.

Days would come and go with the same pale light,
and I learned to make my life small and quiet,
so the wind could slip by without remembering my name.

But seasons are faithful in ways we rarely expect.
One morning,
somewhere beneath thought,
I felt a subtle stirring—the way earth loosens
before the first shoots dare to find their way.

I didn’t do anything.
I simply noticed the warmth returning to places long cold.

And slowly,
almost shyly,
the world began to notice me back—
the sun lingering on my sleeve,
a bird landing close enough for its small weight
to be understood,
the river reflecting not just itself but the shape of me
leaning over its surface.

Now, when I walk the field at dusk,
the grasses part around me as though making room;
the horizon feels wide enough to carry my footsteps;
the sky meets my eyes without looking past them.

I move with a kind of quiet certainty,
not louder,
not brighter—simply here,
fully included in the great conversation of things.

And sometimes,
as the last light lifts from the edges of the day,
I feel myself held by everything I once thought
couldn’t see me—as if the world
had been waiting all along for me to arrive.

After the comparison quieted

There came a morning when I noticed the world
was no longer a ladder.
No rungs.
No climbing.
Just the soft slope of a hillside breathing under a pale sky.

I stood there, unsure at first —
my body still shaped by years of reaching,
measuring,
trying to earn a place that was never taken from me.

But the wind moved through the grass
without preference,
and something in me
leaned toward its honesty.

I felt the spine lift,
not in pride,
but in recognition.
A widening in the ribs,
as if space had always been mine
and I was only now remembering.

The old vigilance loosened.
The scanning fell away.
And in the quiet that followed I found myself belonging
in a way ambition never gave me.

No one was ahead.
No one behind.
Even the horizon seemed to rest.

I walked a few steps forward — not to prove,
not to stand out,
but simply because I had a life to move into.

And in the hush of that small movement
I heard a truth that felt like home:
My presence is already enough.

The world did not need me to rise above it.
It needed me to stand in it fully.

[fusion_builder_container type="flex" hundred_percent="no" equal_height_columns="no" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" background_position="center center" background_repeat="no-repeat" fade="no" background_parallax="none" parallax_speed="0.3" video_aspect_ratio="16:9" video_loop="yes" video_mute="yes" border_style="solid"][fusion_builder_row][fusion_builder_column type="1_1" layout="1_1" background_position="left top" border_style="solid" border_position="all" spacing="yes" background_repeat="no-repeat" margin_top="0px" margin_bottom="0px" animation_speed="0.3" animation_direction="left" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" center_content="no" last="true" hover_type="none" background_blend_mode="overlay" first="true"][fusion_text animation_direction="left" animation_speed="0.3" animation_delay="0" hide_on_mobile="small-visibility,medium-visibility,large-visibility" sticky_display="normal,sticky"]
